To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: [d11]
Cc: none
Subject: Casuals' pay, Embakasi, Monday 30 Nov — what to say, what to promise, and if the Kisumu loading stops (DRAFT — for Achieng)

DRAFT — do not circulate to Brian until I have read it. Saturday 28 November, 9:40pm.

CASUALS' PAY, EMBAKASI — MONDAY 30 NOVEMBER
Briefing note for Brian Ochieng, Operations Manager
Written by Achieng Otieno, HR Manager (I am on the 07:05 to Entebbe, back Wednesday evening)
Read time: about ten minutes. Keep this on your phone on Monday.

1. THE SHORT VERSION
- Friday's pay did not go out. Not partly, not for some people. Nobody on the affected list has been paid for that fortnight.
- The cause is ours, in our back office. Nothing anyone on the yard did caused this, and nobody has done anything wrong.
- Money will be on their phones by M-Pesa on Monday morning, by 11am. Not by bank transfer this time.
- KES 500 lunch money plus fare for every casual on the affected list, in the same M-Pesa batch. Approved by the MD on Saturday.
- You apologise in person on Monday morning, before loading, not after.
- If Ouma's group refuses to load the Kisumu trucks: Ops and HR handle it together, and nobody is threatened or dismissed on the day.

2. WHAT REALLY HAPPENED (the facts, in order — in case you are asked)
a) Casuals are paid fortnightly on Fridays. Friday 27 November's run was 212 records, KES 1,846,300.
b) The bank upgraded its platform on 25 November and required a new file template. We still submitted the old template, so column 7 (beneficiary reference) ran over 20 characters and the file was rejected at validation.
c) Nothing in that file was processed. So nobody has been paid and nobody has been short-paid — every casual on the affected list is in exactly the same position.
d) The bank's cut-off had passed by the time the rejection was picked up (the alert went to an old finance mailbox). There was no time to correct and resubmit on Friday.
e) Decision: skip the bank and push the whole lot through M-Pesa bulk (B2C). The MD approved it Saturday morning, including the top-up the M-Pesa route needs.
f) Numbers are now being checked by a person, not by a file. Peninah has been through the list: 198 confirmed, 14 she could not reach, mostly the new loaders from the Athi River intake.
g) Kevin's realistic estimate: money on phones Monday by 11am. He has not promised earlier and neither should you.
h) The MD also approved KES 500 per head for Monday lunch plus fare for every casual on the affected list, in the same batch, and confirmed the M-Pesa charges are on us. Nobody has a shilling deducted.

3. WHAT YOU CAN PROMISE — AND THE WORDS TO USE
- "Your money is coming by M-Pesa to your phone today, by 11 o'clock." Say 11. Say "this morning" only if you also say 11. Never "by lunch". Never "tomorrow".
- "Nobody's pay is short. What you were owed on Friday is what you will get. The M-Pesa charges are ours — nothing is taken from you."
- "The company has approved 500 shillings for lunch and your fare for today, in the same batch." You can state this as approved.
- "Peninah is here from 7:30 with the list and a laptop. If your number is wrong or you are new, she will fix it with you face to face, and she can print your payslip."
- "Management is sorry, and I am here to say it in person this morning."
- "Nobody is being dismissed or threatened over this. That is the procedure and I am not going to threaten anyone."
- "If you have a complaint, give it to Joseph or to me and HR will answer you in writing within 48 hours." The procedure commits us to the 48 hours, so you can say it.

4. WHAT YOU MUST NOT PROMISE
- Any time earlier than 11am. If pushed for 9: "11 is the time the payment people will stand behind. I am not going to give you a time we cannot keep."
- That the 14 we could not reach will definitely have money at 11am. They can only be paid once they give us a working number. Get them to Peninah before 8:30 so they can go in the same run.
- That this will never happen again. You can say what has changed: a person checks every number before the run, and we pay through M-Pesa instead of a file we do not control. Do not swear to the future.
- Anything about contracts, deductions or job security — not on Monday, and not quietly either. Procedure v3: no dismissal or threat of dismissal on the day.
- Anything about the company's finances. That is not yours to discuss and it is not part of this brief. If someone asks, say: "That is not what this is about. It is a template error on our side, it is being fixed today, and your money comes at 11." Do not confirm, deny or speculate on anything else.
- Anything to Ouma privately that is not on the list above. If he asks for more, say "let me check and come back to you" — and come back to me or Kevin.
- Do not name individuals or blame the finance team in front of the group. Own it at management level: our mistake.
- Do not argue about what was said last time. Agree with it: "Yes, last time we said tomorrow for three days. That was us. We are not doing that today."

5. THE MOMENT TO BE CAREFUL ABOUT (Mombasa, 2024)
Mombasa, 2024: you were told "by lunch". The money came at 4pm and half the shift sat down and stayed down. We are not repeating that.
The rule now: one time, said clearly, and told the truth about it before it slips. If at 10:00 the batch has not gone out, you go back to the group before 10:30 with a new time you can keep, even if that is "12:30". It was the silence that broke trust last time, not the delay.

6. MONDAY'S TIMELINE
- 05:30 — you are at the depot (your plan, keep it).
- Before 06:00 — tell Joseph the plan. He has been holding this yard together since yesterday and he asked who is coming to talk to them. Give him the briefing order and the 11am message so he is never caught flat-footed.
- 05:45 at the latest — WhatsApp me two lines. I am up from 4:30 and boarding around 06:30, so a message before then still reaches me. If there is a stoppage, call me, not just WhatsApp; if I am already in the air, call Kevin and NW so we can get HR on the phone with you.
- 06:00–06:30, or the moment he arrives — Ouma, privately, before the group. Section 7.
- 07:30 — Peninah on site with the printout and laptop. Start with the 14 unreachable; hard deadline 08:30 for their numbers so they can go into the same run.
- 08:15 — group briefing and your apology, in person, before loading starts.
- 08:30–08:50 — loading under way, Joseph with the group.
- 09:00 — Kisumu trucks must leave to make the offloading slot at the mill.
- 11:00 — money lands. Have someone at the gate with the run list, ready to check names and numbers. Anyone saying "nothing arrived" goes to Peninah with his phone; do not argue at the gate. Tell them to keep the phone on and check M-Pesa balance (dial *334#).
- If the trucks will be late, call the mill early so you do not lose the slot by silence.

7. OUMA
He is loud, and he is not a bad man. Four children, rent due on the 1st. He is carrying the mood of the yard and he is carrying his own worry.
- Speak to him first, alone, before the whole group hears anything — away from the others, early, before he has time to build a crowd around himself.
- Do not open with the schedule. Open with the error: our file, our mistake, nobody on this yard did anything wrong.
- Give him facts he can check: Peninah here from 7:30, money on phones by 11, lunch and fare money included, no deductions, nobody threatened.
- Ask him what his people need in order to load safely on Monday, and write it down.
- Ask him to pass the message on. Do not put words in his mouth and do not make him a guarantor for management.
- Keep it straight, not soft. He will respect that. What he will not accept is being handled.

8. IF OUMA'S GROUP REFUSES TO LOAD
First, to yourself: no threats, no contracts, no dismissals, no police, no forcing the gate. Procedure v3 — a stoppage is not a grievance channel, it is handled by Operations and HR together, and no one is to be dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day. It is also not ours to settle between us: I am the HR half of that procedure and I am on a plane, so you must not handle it alone.
1. Reach me on WhatsApp immediately, and call if you can. If I am airborne, call Kevin and NW and ask for HR to join by phone. Do not proceed without HR.
2. Talk to Ouma again, privately, the same way as before. Ask what would make it safe to load.
3. Move the grievances into the proper channel: Joseph writes down names, times and requests; HR answers in writing within 48 hours. That gives the men something real and stops the stoppage being the negotiation.
4. If loading has started, let it continue. Note who is not loading and do not confront anyone. If nothing has moved by 08:40, call me, Kevin or NW for a joint call with Ouma's group at 08:45.
5. Protect the mill slot — if the trucks will be late, call Kisumu early.
6. Write it down as it happens: times, who was there, what was said, what was asked for. Send it to me and HR the same day. Any disciplinary step is a separate matter, later, in writing, through HR — not on the yard on Monday.

9. YOUR APOLOGY, IN ABOUT 30 SECONDS
"Before we start loading, listen. On Friday our pay file was rejected by the bank because of a change on their side we did not catch. That is our mistake. None of you did anything wrong. And there is no excuse for three days of 'tomorrow' last time — that was management failing to keep a word to you. I am sorry. Today the money goes by M-Pesa to your phones by 11 o'clock. Every one of you on the list — including the 14 we could not reach on the phone, because the numbers are wrong, not because you are forgotten. Peninah is here from 7:30 with the list and the laptop; come and fix yours with her. The company has also approved 500 for lunch and your fare today, in the same batch, and nothing is deducted from anyone's pay. If your number or phone is wrong, tell Peninah now, not at 11 o'clock. If you have a complaint, give it to Joseph or to me and HR will answer you in writing within 48 hours. And nobody is being dismissed or threatened today."

10. IF ANYTHING CHANGES
WhatsApp me before I board. Two lines is enough. What I need to know: did Ouma speak; did the group accept 11am; did the 14 numbers come through; has loading started; has the payment run been submitted. If nothing has changed by 06:00, send "all as planned" so I know you have what you need.

11. ONE-PAGE VERSION (screenshot this)
- Money: by M-Pesa to phones, Monday, 11am. Say 11. Never "by lunch", never earlier.
- Cause: our file rejected after the bank system change. Nobody's fault but ours.
- Extra: KES 500 lunch + fare, same batch. No deductions, M-Pesa charges are ours.
- Apology: in person, 08:15, before loading.
- Ouma: alone, first, before the group. Facts, not a speech.
- 14 unreachable: Peninah, 7:30, numbers by 08:30 or they wait for the next run.
- Procedure: stoppage = Ops + HR together. No threats, no dismissals, no police.
- Trucks: leave by 09:00. Escalate by 08:40 if nothing has moved.
- Me: WhatsApp before 06:30 — I am up from 4:30. Call if I am airborne.
- Do not discuss company finances. If asked: "not what this is about, your money comes at 11."
- Anything still open Wednesday, when I am back, we take up properly.

One last thing from me: you have done this six years and you will read this better than any brief I can write. The only instruction I want underlined is the 11am — and the promise to tell them early if it moves. That is the only thing that will cost us the yard on Monday.

reasons: It incorrectly promises a written HR response within 48 hours and treats fare as additional to the approved KES 500.
